text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KONTINENT
-- Bulgaria's President Petar Stoyanov said his country expected no miracles from the Madrid summit but was not going to give up its efforts for NATO membership with the first obstacle.

Stoyanov, who is leaving today for Madrid where he is to meet U.S. President Bill Clinton, said Bulgaria's clear statement on NATO membership had been late but his country was to make up lost time with a 'Bulgarian storm'.
24 CHASA

-- Bulgaria's cabinet approved a draft bill aimed at opening secret files of the communist era State Security Service in a bid to avoid further speculation and prevent attempts to blackmail politicians.
The draft, which is yet to be passed by the parliament, is expected to be voted and come into force by the end of August.
TRUD
-- Foreign trade turnover between Bulgaria and Greece ammounted to $519 million in 1996, down from $621 million in the previous year, head of Bulgaria's Chamber of Commerce Bozhidar Bozhinov said.

He said that some 800 Greek companies were registered in Bulgaria and nearly half of them were 100 percent Greek-owned. The turnover for the first quarter of 1997 between the two neighbouring Balkan states was $136 million, he added.
-- The U.S. computer giant IBM has offered Bulgaria a $100 million loan for setting up computer networks for tax, customs, social insurance services and bank supervision, the president's office said.
STANDART

-- Bulgaria's government decided to replace its two representatives appointed by the former Socialist government in the supervisory board of the Bulgarian-Russian gas company Topenergy but the changes are yet to be voted at an extraordinary shareholders' meeting of the company in August.
-- Greek companies have shown interest in the sell-offs Bulgaria's biggest steel works Kremikovtsi and the state tobacco monopolost Bulgartabac Holding, Bulgaria's Chamber of Commerce said.
NOVINAR

-- The leader of Bulgaria's ethnic Turks Movement for Rights and Freedoms Ahmed Dogan said he was going to lobby in the parliament for the country's biggest comglomerate Multigroup, saying the business activities of the private grouping were favourable for the country's econommy.
PARI

-- The assets and liabilities of the central bank Issue Department rose to three billion marks from 2.8 billion marks a week ago, when Bulgaria launched a fixed exchange rate regime, known as currency board, the central bank said.

-- Bulgaria posted a capital and financial account deficit of 101.2 million in the first quarter of 1997 after a surplus of $217.1 million in the same period the previous year, central bank preliminary figures show,
